key_insight: UniX reconciles the conflicting goals of semantic abstraction and pixel-accurate reconstruction by combining autoregressive and diffusion paradigms in one unified chest X‑ray foundation model, avoiding the performance trade-offs of parameter-sharing designs.
problem_solved: Existing unified medical models struggle because autoregressive sharing forces a single pathway to serve both high-level understanding and low-level image generation, degrading one or both capabilities; UniX eliminates this conflict.
method: Hybrid architecture: a shared visual encoder with two specialized branches — an autoregressive branch for semantic understanding and a diffusion branch for high‑fidelity image generation.
Task‑specific decoders and loss functions to decouple semantic abstraction from pixel reconstruction while enabling cross-task knowledge transfer.
Joint training strategy that balances objectives and reduces parameter interference (e.g., regularization or cross-attention gating between branches).
impact: UniX enables a single foundation model that performs strongly on both diagnostic tasks (reports/labels) and realistic image generation, simplifying deployment, improving data augmentation, and advancing clinical AI workflows.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: shared encoder feeding two clearly labeled branches (autoregressive → semantics; diffusion → pixels).
Side-by-side examples: original chest X-ray, generated/reconstructed image, and generated report/label to show dual capabilities.
Bar chart: comparative metrics showing improvements on both understanding (e.g., AUC/F1) and generation (e.g., FID/LPIPS) versus prior unified and single-task baselines.
Training flowchart: losses and gating/regularization components that prevent parameter conflict between branches.
paper_title: UniX: Unifying Autoregression and Diffusion for Chest X-Ray Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ruiheng Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Huangxuan Zhao, Hao Yan, Xiao He
